title: Noeul IPC v1 message
description: One JSON frame between the noeul CLI and the running Noeul instance (4-byte little-endian length, then the UTF-8 JSON object; at most 65536 bytes). See docs/adr/0023-noeul-app-foundation.md §4, docs/adr/0029-noeul-pin-engine.md (pin methods, Step 53), docs/adr/0044-noeul-pin-transforms-and-control.md (pin.set, groups, Step 54) and crates/noeul/src/ipc.rs. Errors carry registered CLI error codes (docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md §6). Pictures never cross the pipe; results carry IDs, geometry and counts only (NOEUL-SEC-008).

error_code.description: Registered CLI error codes the instance may answer with.

point.description: A point in device pixels of the virtual desktop.

zoom.description: Pin zoom in percent; 100 = one image pixel per device pixel (Step 53); any whole percent since border resizing (Step 54).

opacity.description: Pin opacity in percent; never below 10 (Step 54, NOEUL-FR-062).

group_name.description: A pin group (Step 54): 1–32 letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `_` or `.`, starting with a letter or digit.

orientation.description: How a pin is turned (Step 54): mirrored left-right first, then rotated clockwise.

rect.description: Device pixels of the virtual desktop.

connection_error.description: Sent instead of a welcome (refused handshake) or after a malformed frame; the sender closes the connection.

params.description: Parameters of every method (absent flags are false). capture: exactly one of region, monitor or window (monitor and window since Step 58), pin (required) and pointer; capture.region and capture.cancel: dry_run only; pin.create: source (region with region, clipboard with an optional at and as, or file with path and an optional at; Step 55); pin.hide, pin.show, pin.close and pin.set: id, group or all; pin.show: on_screen; pin.set: at (one pin), zoom, opacity, rotation, mirrored, rotate, flip, thumbnail, click_through, move_to_group (Step 54); group.switch: group; history.pin and history.forget: entry (Step 60); quit: force.

output.description: capture (Step 62): write the capture to this absolute .png path on a local drive instead of pinning it.

replace.description: capture with output: write over an existing file.

via.description: Step 62: `mcp` when an agent asks through `noeul mcp serve` (the privacy setting privacy.mcp_captures applies); absent: the CLI or another IPC client (privacy.cli applies).

entry.description: history.pin (default: the newest) and history.forget: a kept capture's number (Step 60).

monitor.description: capture: a whole monitor — the primary one, the one under the pointer, or the n-th in the order `status` lists them (Step 58, NOEUL-FR-017).

window.description: capture: the window that has the keyboard focus, as the user sees it on screen (Step 58, NOEUL-FR-017).

pointer.description: capture: draw the mouse pointer into the picture (Step 58, NOEUL-FR-016).

source.description: pin.create: what the instance reads itself (Step 53; file since Step 55).

as.description: pin.create with source clipboard: pin this kind instead of the first one the clipboard offers (Step 55, NOEUL-FR-071).

path.description: pin.create with source file: an absolute local path to an image file (Step 55, NOEUL-FR-073); never echoed in a result.

at.description: pin.create with source clipboard: where the picture's top-left corner goes (default: the pointer); pin.set: where one pin's picture goes exactly (Step 54).

on_screen.description: pin.show: also move pins no monitor shows into the nearest work area (NOEUL-FR-067).

group.description: pin.hide, pin.show, pin.close and pin.set: every pin of this group; group.switch: the group to switch to (Step 54, NOEUL-FR-064).

rotation.description: pin.set: the rotation in degrees clockwise (absolute).

mirrored.description: pin.set: mirrored left-right before the rotation (absolute).

rotate.description: pin.set: a quarter turn right (cw) or left (ccw), after rotation and mirrored.

flip.description: pin.set: a flip as shown, after rotate.

thumbnail.description: pin.set: thumbnail mode on or off.

click_through.description: pin.set: let mouse clicks pass through the pins (NOEUL-FR-063); the CLI's caller keeps the CLI as its way back.

filter.description: pin.set (#99): how the pins show their colours (the view only).

sharp.description: pin.set (#99): sharp pixels when zoomed out.

topmost.description: pin.set (#99): above other windows or in the normal z-order.

color.description: pin.set (#99, `COLOR-05`): a colour card's new colour (HEX, rgb() or hsl()); other pins are left alone.

move_to_group.description: pin.set: move the pins to this group.

seconds.description: hotkeys.pause (ADR 0093): release the global hotkeys for this many seconds (at most 120) while the settings window records keys; 0 registers them again now.

dpi.description: Effective DPI (96 = 100 %); every rectangle is in device pixels (Step 50).

work.description: The work area: the monitor without the taskbar and docked bars; pins are placed inside it (Step 53).

rotation.description: How the monitor is turned, degrees clockwise; rect is already the turned size (Step 58).

hdr.description: Advanced colour (HDR, or wide colour enforced) is on; null when unknown. Windows converts captures of such a monitor to SDR (Step 58, NOEUL-FR-092).

hotkeys_state.description: Global shortcut state of the running instance (or, offline, from the files). Conflicts are hotkeys-cli-v1 conflict objects.

language.description: `[general] language` (#99, SET-21): the tray menu's and the pin menu's language; `auto` follows the Windows display language.

tray_clicks.description: `[general] tray_left_click` and `tray_middle_click` (#99): what a left or middle click on the tray icon does; the right click is the menu.

keyboard_help.description: `[capture] keyboard_help`: when the capture overlay shows its keyboard help (Step 50).

quick_save_folder.description: `[capture] quick_save_folder` (Step 51); null: the Pictures folder + Noeul.

detection.description: `[capture] detection` (Step 52, NOEUL-FR-040): what the overlay detects under the pointer when it opens.

magnifier.description: `[capture] magnifier` (Step 52, NOEUL-FR-041): whether the overlay shows the magnifier when it opens.

pointer.description: `[capture] pointer` (Step 58, NOEUL-FR-016): whether the mouse pointer is drawn into the pictures F1, capture.monitor and capture.window take.

pins.description: `[pins]` (Step 54, UX spec §10): the outline and the shadow around every pin; `backup` (Step 60, NOEUL-FR-066): the opt-in pin backup; `double_click` (ADR 0094): a double-click on a pin closes it (`close`, the default) or does nothing.

privacy.description: `[privacy]` (Step 62, NOEUL-SEC-010): CLI and IPC captures and clipboard reads notify (default), are allowed silently or denied; agent (MCP) captures are off unless turned on.

history.description: `[history]` (Step 60, NOEUL-FR-050, NOEUL-FR-051): how many earlier captures and how much memory, whether they are also kept on disk and for how long, whether cancelled captures are kept.

auto_save.description: #99 (`HIST-06`): every pinned or copied capture is also saved into the quick-save folder (never a private one); off by default.

output.description: `[output]` (#99): the format of quick saves and auto-saves (`png` lossless, or `jpeg` at `jpeg_quality`; a save to a `.jpg` file is JPEG too), and whether a copy also puts the picture on the clipboard as a file (a PNG in Noeul's own folder, removed at quit).

paste.description: `[paste]` (Step 55, NOEUL-FR-071): whether a copied path to an image file pins the file, and whether copied non-image files become a card of their names.

color.description: `[color]` (Step 59, NOEUL-FR-044): the colour picker's format when a capture starts, the HEX case and whether the alpha is included.

gestures.description: `[gestures]` (Step 51, NOEUL-FR-024): what a double-click and a middle-click inside a confirmed selection do, and the preset's name.

status_result.description: `status`. Also the `data` of `noeul status --json` while Noeul runs.

capture_backend.description: `synthetic` only in a debug build with the test hook NOEUL_DEV_SYNTHETIC_DESKTOP (ADR 0026).

off_screen.description: Open pins no monitor shows enough of to reach, e.g. after a monitor was removed (Step 53, NOEUL-FR-067).

click_through.description: Open pins that let mouse clicks pass through (Step 54, NOEUL-FR-063).

group.description: The current group: new pins go to it (Step 54).

groups.description: How many groups there are, the current one included.

editor.description: The annotation editor of a pin (`pin.annotate`, Step 56), while one is open.

saved.description: Captures that ended with Save or quick save (Step 51).

colors.description: Captures that ended with the colour picker's `color.copy` (Step 59); a count only, never a colour.

ignored.description: Capture requests that found an overlay open and did nothing (NOEUL-FR-013).

history.description: Rectangles of earlier successful captures kept in memory for `history.previous`/`history.next` (Step 52, NOEUL-FR-050; at most 20, never on disk).

memory.description: Image buffers the instance holds (frames and bytes), a local metric (ADR 0012).

displays.description: Display notifications (WM_DISPLAYCHANGE, work-area changes, WM_DPICHANGED) received, and how often the instance looked at the displays: once per quiet period of 250 ms, at most 1 s after the first (Step 58, ADR 0050).

offline_status.description: The `data` of `noeul status --json` when no instance runs (not an IPC message).

clickable.description: Pins that let clicks through and were made clickable again by this second start (Step 54, NOEUL-FR-063).

rect.description: The picture on screen: position and shown size (at its zoom, turned, or the thumbnail); the window adds the outline and shadow around it.

capture_result.description: `capture`: a region, a monitor or the active window, captured without the overlay and pinned in place (or, since Step 62, written to a PNG file: `file`) (monitor, window, pointer, mapping and warnings since Step 58, ADR 0050). Geometry and states only: never pixels, a window title or a program name.

file.description: Step 62: written to the file the request named (`output`) instead of pinned; the path is never echoed.

region.description: What was (or would be) captured, in device pixels of the virtual desktop.

monitor.description: The monitor that holds the region's centre (the reference of `mapping`).

number.description: 1-based, in the order `status` lists the monitors.

mapping.description: The region in the logical pixels of that monitor, relative to its top-left corner (each edge rounded on its own), how many monitors it touches and whether their scales differ (the picture keeps every monitor's device pixels).

window.description: target window: its visible frame (DWM extended frame bounds) and capture affinity; `region` is the part of it on the monitors.

pointer.description: null unless the pointer was asked for; then whether it was drawn, where its image lies, or why not.

warnings.description: Honest limits of this capture: monitors of different scales, HDR converted to SDR, a window that protects itself or lies partly off the monitors, a pointer not in the picture.

annotation_state.description: The overlay's annotations (Step 56, NOEUL-FR-080/081; the privacy tools mosaic, blur, eraser and solid redaction since Step 57, NOEUL-FR-082): the tool, counts, IDs and style only, never the text of a label, a point, a pixel or what a redaction covers (NOEUL-SEC-008).

kinds.description: How many objects of each kind.

double-arrow.description: #99 (ANN-12): arrows with a head at both ends.

editing_text.description: A label is being edited (every other shortcut is suspended).

composing.description: An input-method composition is shown in the label.

color.description: The colour new objects of the current tool get (the redaction tool keeps its own, black by default).

width.description: The line width in logical pixels.

overlay_state.description: The open capture overlay (Step 50, ADR 0026): geometry and state only, never pixels, colours, window titles or element names (NOEUL-SEC-007, NOEUL-SEC-008).

session.description: The capture session; 0 while a pin is edited.

mode.description: `capture`: the region capture overlay; `pin_edit`: a pin's annotation editor (Step 56).

pin.description: The pin being edited (`pin_edit`), else null.

phase.description: `marking`: the first corner was set with `selection.mark` (Step 52). `annotating`: a drawing tool is active, a label is edited or a stroke is drawn (Step 56).

focus.description: What has the keyboard focus (Step 51): the canvas or a toolbar button (the annotation buttons since Step 56, the privacy tools since Step 57).

pointer.description: Where the overlay's pointer is (Step 52; moved by the mouse or the pointer keys).

detection.description: Hover detection (Step 52, NOEUL-FR-040, ADR 0035): rectangles only.

windows.description: Windows detection offers in this capture; null: no window list (detection off since the overlay opened, or the list could not be read).

target.description: What a click or `selection.mark` would select now; null when nothing is detected.

protected.description: The pointer is over a window protected from capture (WDA_MONITOR): Windows captures it black; it is never highlighted (NOEUL-SEC-004).

fallback.description: Why the last element lookup used the window rectangle.

suspended.description: The keyboard moved the pointer last: detection and snapping pause until the mouse moves.

magnifier.description: The magnifier (Step 52, NOEUL-FR-041); its colour readout is drawn, never reported.

color.description: The colour picker (Step 59, NOEUL-FR-044): the format `color.copy` copies now, the HEX case and whether the alpha is included. Never the colour under the pointer (NOEUL-SEC-008).

history.description: `history.previous`/`history.next` (Step 52): rectangles kept for this overlay and the one shown (0 = oldest).

first_frame.description: First-frame latency of the overlay (request to overlay painted, NOEUL-NFR-003), a local metric (ADR 0012). Percentiles cover the last 100 captures.

capture_region_result.description: `capture.region`: open the selection overlay, as F1 does. `opened` is false for a dry run and while an overlay is already open (`reason: already_open`).

capture_cancel_result.description: `capture.cancel`: close an open overlay without pinning, copying or saving anything.

rect.description: The picture on screen: position and shown size (at its zoom, turned, or the thumbnail); the window adds the outline and shadow around it.

image.description: The picture's size in pixels (100 %, as captured, before any rotation).

visible.description: False while the pin is hidden (Step 53).

on_screen.description: Whether a monitor shows enough of the pin to reach it; null while the desktop is not available (Step 53).

annotations.description: Annotations the pin carries as editable objects (Step 56).

editing.description: Its annotations are being edited (its window is hidden meanwhile).

thumbnail.description: Thumbnail mode: `rect` is the thumbnail, `zoom` waits for when it ends (Step 54).

click_through.description: Mouse clicks pass through it (Step 54, NOEUL-FR-063).

filter.description: #99: how it shows its colours (the view only; copy and save keep them).

topmost.description: #99: above other windows (the default) or in the normal z-order.

selected.description: #99 (`PIN-20`): selected with other pins (`Ctrl`+click, `pin.select-all`); a pin action on it acts on every selected pin.

animation.description: Made from an animated GIF, of which it shows only the first frame (NOEUL-FR-068: never flattened silently); null otherwise.

content.description: What the pin shows (Step 55): a picture, or a card made from text, HTML, a colour value or file names; never the content itself.

pin_set_result.description: `pin.set` (Step 54): the pins named, the ones that changed (none for a dry run) and how they are now.

group_list_result.description: `group.list` (Step 54): every group with open pins and the current one.

group_switch_result.description: `group.switch` (Step 54): the pins shown and hidden by the switch (or that would be, in a dry run).

pin_create_result.description: `pin.create` (Step 53): the instance captured the region or read the clipboard or the file itself; `pin` is null for a dry run, which captures and reads nothing. Since Step 55 a clipboard or file pin also says what it pinned: `kind`, every kind the clipboard offered (`offered`, names only), all the pins it made (`pins`, the first is `pin`) and how many offered files were skipped or failed.

paste_kind.description: What a paste pins (Step 55, NOEUL-FR-071), in priority order: an image, image files, a colour value, HTML, plain text, file names.

pin_hide_result.description: `pin.hide` (Step 53): the pins that were (or, in a dry run, would be) hidden; pins hidden already are not listed.

pin_show_result.description: `pin.show` (Step 53): the pins that were shown again, and (with on_screen) moved into a work area.

settings_open_result.description: settings.open (Step 61): the settings window opened or brought forward (never by another method).

history_list_result.description: history.list (Step 60, NOEUL-FR-050): the kept captures, oldest first — geometry, time and outcome only, never pixels.

hotkeys_pause_result.description: `hotkeys.pause` (ADR 0093): the global hotkeys are released until `seconds` pass or a pause of 0 resumes them (`resumed`: they were paused).

settings_reload_result.description: `settings.reload` (Step 51): config.toml read again; the gestures, keyboard help and quick-save folder apply from the next capture.
